body: Do not use `syntax on` and `filetype on` with Neovim; they're enabled by default and not idempotent (they're commands, not options!).

If the difference persists even without `syntax on filetype on`, this is likely due to `filetype.lua` having to check the full contents of your huge file to determine the filetype. Would be useful to profile `filetype/detect.lua` in this case (simply sprinkling `print os.time()` through the file) to see where the slowdown is and see what `scripts.vim` (which should be functionally identical) is doing differently.

@smjonas
@osthomas It looks like your file is all in one line -- does it make a difference if you have many (short) lines?

Thanks for looking into this!

@clason 
The test file from the script above is not on one line on my end, and the file I initially noticed this on likewise has many lines. So no, this is not dependent on the file being a single line. Having only one huge line might make it worse, though, I have not tested that.

Also, I get the same behavior with just `--clean` without the additional `-u`.
I see, thanks. Then I suspect that we've been to cavalier in checking all lines where `scripts.vim` only checks the first 1000 or so.

So it's definitely related to looping over all lines somewhere, not `string.find` performance (which is good news!) (You don't need to keep testing the full matrix; the only important difference is between `nvim --clean` on 0.7.2 and master.)

@osthomas if you want to help bisect, you can start with removing in turn the two `match_from_foo` functions here:
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/f5588ee8968c564f6f7b0e42ac0ad44f83489659/runtime/lua/vim/filetype/detect.lua#L1632-L1639


Depending on which of these the slowdown comes from, the next step is to bisect the pattern tables
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/f5588ee8968c564f6f7b0e42ac0ad44f83489659/runtime/lua/vim/filetype/detect.lua#L1455-L1574
and https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/f5588ee8968c564f6f7b0e42ac0ad44f83489659/runtime/lua/vim/filetype/detect.lua#L1358-L1396
(my suspicion is the former).

Reminder: if you edit the Lua runtime files, you can then test with `VIMRUNTIME=./runtime build/bin/nvim` without having to install.
Does it? I think it re-grabs the contents in `scripts.vim`?

> Does it? I think it re-grabs the contents in `scripts.vim`?

Pretty sure, yes. There are separate variables for lines 1 to 5 only.

@smjonas the biggest culprit is, hardly surprisingly,
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/f5588ee8968c564f6f7b0e42ac0ad44f83489659/runtime/lua/vim/filetype/detect.lua#L1583-L1586
I think it would make sense to limit this to a small subset of the lines.

**EDIT** Using `table.concat(contents, '\n', 1, 5)` is faster but only by 40%; need to find other bottle necks.

> Pretty sure, yes. There are separate variables for lines 1 to 5 only.

Not quite; there are also functions (most notably "CVS diff") that grab the last line or iterate over all lines themselves.
